verdict:
THE ORIGINAL KILL IS UNVERIFIED, BY ITS OWN SCALE ERROR. It compares a paired mean over 967 prompts (-0.2083) against a per-prompt range over 20 draws (2.2378) and fired W3; the paired CI is [-0.2513, -0.1653] and excludes zero, which reads W2. A mean and an extreme order statistic are not comparable -- the same defect this repository added to realstat as 'min/max of N draws quoted as an interval' three commits ago. Neither reading is admissible and the W2/W3 question is settled by the W4 arm instead.

  WHAT IS ESTABLISHED REGARDLESS, and it is what the certificate needed: of 3.95 criteria printed per core, 1.45 are NECESSARY-WITHIN-SET (36.7%) and the smallest subset reproducing the printed core's own class is 1.42. On 23.8% of prompts ZERO printed criteria are necessary; on 5.4% all are. The `representative` field can be issued from these numbers today.

  W4: W4 CONFIRMED -- generic text explains it: the generic vocabulary is as redundant as the printed core (+0.0042, CI contains 0) while full-rubric random is not (+0.2500). The compiler's redundancy is inherited from WRITING GENERIC CRITERIA, not from which criteria it chose.
